transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-18
Start: 09:30 PDT
Duration: 75 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Sofia Morales, Evan Li, Priya Shah, Darren Bailey, Ravi Kapoor, Maya Gomez, Anita Reyes, Tom Nguyen
Shared: launch gate deck (https://redwood.internal/launch-gate-deck), canary checklist spreadsheet (link: /sheets/canary-2026-09), SOC2 snippets (drive: /security/soc2-launch)

[00:00] Sofia: Ok, cool, good morning everyone. We'll kick off — this is the critical path stability and sprint-gate review. Short agenda: canary plan, security gating, QA/regressions, networking, and rollback. We're time boxed to an hour and a quarter.

[00:22] Evan: Hey — quick status: infra build is green, most kernels landed yesterday. There's still that quant-kernel fallback issue on the A100s where memory spikes at ~1.2x expected for long sequences. We've got a mitigation patch but it's unverified in perf runs.

[00:45] Priya: To add — SLOs look fine in staging but the KV cache warm-up pattern causes a 200–400ms tail when prefixes aren't cached. That tail impacts median for certain flows. We need to decide if we accept a temporary tail or push a caching pre-warm.

[01:10] Darren: From QA, our regression suite is at 86% pass. The failing tests are mostly flaky conversational reranking tests and one load scenario that times out intermittently. I don't think they're blocking but they do raise false-alert noise during canary.

[01:35] Sofia: Let's go through the checklist. Evan, canary ramp — what percent and what metrics do you want to be green before we open more traffic?

[01:48] Evan: Proposal: start with 1% for two hours, 5% for four hours, 10% for 24 hours if all green. Success metrics: p50/p95 latency under target (+10% buffer), error rate <0.2% (user-facing errors), token cost within expected budget. Also watch model fallback counts and kernel fallback rate.

[02:12] Maya: Will we split traffic by customer tier? for the pilot we said only internal test tenants and a few opt-ins, right?

[02:25] Sofia: Correct — internal tenants + pilot partners. Not global production.

[02:40] Anita: Security note — KMS rotation check. Last rotation introduced an outage in previous rollout. We need a dry run of key rollover in staging with a rollback plan. Also audit logs must be flowing to the audit bucket and be immutable for the pilot timeframe.

[02:58] Ravi: On that, VPC peering and private endpoint verification — I've validated the peering for us-west-2 but not yet for eu-west-1. The on-prem private deployment pack has a couple small iptables rules differences that may cause connectivity flaps under load. I'll finish the eu-west checks by EOD Friday.

[03:25] Priya: Another SRE concern: backup route for model-mesh. If the primary cluster saturates, we want automatic fallback to a lower-cost quantized variant but only after X% queue depth. That behavior needs to be simulated now — not in production.

[03:48] Evan: Right, and that touches cost/latency tradeoffs. The quantized variant increases latency by ~30ms median, but halves GPU memory. For some flows that's acceptable. We should document which RPC routes can tolerate the quantized path.

[04:12] Tom: How will we communicate degradation to support? A single incident channel or multiple? I don't want triage to open a hundred noisy tickets from customers.

[04:25] Sophie (sic) [note: transcription mislabel]: Support should have a dedicated pilot status channel and a toggle to mute low-sev alerts during the canary window. Also support playbook link in the deck.

[04:50] Darren: On flaky tests — I propose we quarantine the top 8 flakes and run them in isolation daily. That reduces noise and let's automation focus on real regressions. If they keep failing, we escalate.

[05:12] Sofia: Good. Anything blocking rollbacks? We should confirm rollback script works for model versions and routing policies.

[05:25] Evan: Rollback script exists but we haven't exercised the full end-to-end: model routing + cache invalidation + prefix cache priming. I want to run a simulated rollback in staging where we intentionally break the canary and trigger the fallback. That should be in the canary playbook.

[05:48] Priya: I'll add automated validation that after rollback, KV cache is consistent and no dangling sessions remain. That's the thing that bit us in the last release.

[06:10] Anita: For compliance, please ensure all SSO events are captured with trace IDs so we can map user requests to tokens in the audit logs. We need that baked before pilot since security sign-off depends on it.

[06:32] Evan: Noted. I'll add trace id propagation to the gateway layer in the canary build.

[06:45] Sofia: Ok let's talk acceptance criteria. If the canary meets the metrics Evan stated, QA gives a green on regressions (no criticals), security signs off on SOC2 runbook items, and infra confirms networking, then we go ahead with a limited rollout. If any single gating criterion fails, we hold.

[07:10] Ravi: One more infra risk: node autoscaling in the dedicated pool sometimes undershoots with sustained short bursts due to our autoscaler cooldown. We need a short-term policy tweak to be more aggressive during the canary. I can submit a tweak and roll it to canary only.

[07:33] Evan: Be careful — aggressive autoscaling will increase cost and may mask a real perf regression. Let's keep the change minimal: reduce cooldown from 300s to 120s for the canary window. Monitor cost.

[07:50] Darren: Also QA will simulate spike patterns to validate autoscaler behavior. We'll include the spike profile in the canary checklist spreadsheet.

[08:05] Sofia: Action recap — Evan to run canary ramp, Priya to send SOC2/KMS checklist, Darren to finish regression matrix, Ravi to finish peering checks, Sofia to update the gate doc. Anything else?

[08:22] Maya: Quick ask — can we include a short exec one-pager that highlights residual risk and mitigation steps? Execs want an at-a-glance yes/no recommendation.

[08:35] Sofia: I'll produce a one-pager and a risk table.

[08:47] Anita: Also, re: KMS — add an emergency key revoke and restore play example in the doc. We had one previous incident where rotation timing caused token rejects.

[09:05] Evan: I'll add a small script that simulates revoke/restore in staging without touching production keys.

[09:18] Priya: On monitoring — let's ensure the telemetry includes model-fallback counters, kernel-fallback counters, kv-cache hit ratio by prefix, and slow-tail p99 by route. Those will be useful during canary and immediate rollback decisions.

[09:40] Ravi: Network metrics will include TCP retransmits between peered VPCs and interface queue drops. If we see >1% retransmit we abort the canary.

[09:58] Darren: I want to call out one QA risk: a third-party dependency in the reranker library has a minor patch that changed tie-breaking. It didn't show up in unit tests but caused slightly different order in a small set of prompts. We should run a fidelity check on top customer prompts.

[10:18] Sofia: Good catch — add fidelity check to the canary checklist and compare outputs. That will feed the quality monitoring.

[10:38] Evan: Anything on procurement/legal? Are we clear on the pilot partner contract terms and data retention?

[10:50] Maya: Procurement signed the pilot MOU but legal wants explicit data residency statements for EU tenants. We need a short note in the pilot info sheet.

[11:05] Anita: Add that we mustn't store raw prompts for EU tenants beyond the retention window and use pseudonymization for audit retention. We'll provide the snippet.

[11:22] Sofia: Ok, final recap and owners — we'll attach the canary spreadsheet and an updated launch gate doc in the follow-up email. Plan to start canary Monday 2026-09-21 09:00 PDT pending signoffs. If any gating item fails during the canary, we abort and run rollback as documented.

[11:50] Tom: Support will standby and use the pilot status channel, we'll throttle low severity alerts.

[12:05] Sofia: Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels fuzzy (e.g., Sophie vs Sofia), occasional mis-heard terms (KV cache transcribed as K V cache), proper nouns like kernel fallback sometimes shown as kernel fall back. Links referenced rather than inlined.
